text:
MANILA, Philippines — President Lee Jae Myung highlighted growing public goodwill, expanding economic cooperation and mutually beneficial security ties with Japan during a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Manila, Tuesday.
During their bilateral talks on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit and related gatherings in the Philippines, Lee also said he would accept Takaichi’s invitation to visit Japan in January next year.
It was their first meeting in about six months, bringing their total number of summits to four.
“South Korea-Japan relations are looking brighter than ever,” Lee said, crediting Takaichi’s efforts as he noted that “public perceptions of each other’s countries have improved considerably, perhaps reaching an all-time high.”
The president added that people-to-people exchanges and economic cooperation are expanding, while security ties are benefiting both sides.
Regarding Takaichi's invitation for him to visit in January, he said, “I will gladly visit and look forward to seeing you there.”
The Japanese prime minister stressed the growing importance of bilateral ties as global challenges intensify.
“As the international situation grows increasingly challenging, I believe relations between Japan and South Korea are becoming more important,” she said.
She also recalled her visit to Korea last year, thanking Lee for showing her the country’s scenery and saying she has many fond memories of the experience.
The two leaders first met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, in October 2025.
Their second meeting was held in Takaichi’s hometown of Nara, Japan, in January, and they met a third time in Lee’s hometown of Andong, North Gyeongsang Province, in May.
Tuesday’s summit drew attention for its implications for bilateral relations as well as regional and international affairs, particularly Northeast Asian security, ahead of a planned summit involving the United States, China and Russia on Thursday.
The three-way meeting among U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.
Both Lee and Takaichi will also attend this year’s APEC gathering.
Adding to the regional diplomatic stakes, Trump first floated the idea in August of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un during his Asia tour this month.
Although prospects for such talks have since faded, Trump said Monday that a potential meeting with Kim is up to Xi.
